title: Annual Fee Billing, Waiver and Refund Window on Personal Credit Cards
content:
The tier's annual fee is billed as an annual fee on the statement that closes in the account's anniversary month each year, the anniversary month being the month in which the account was opened.

**Where no annual fee is billed.**

- Where the tier does not charge the annual fee in the first account year, no annual fee is billed on the first anniversary-month statement after opening that falls within twelve months of the opening date.
- No annual fee is billed while the military rate cap is in force on the account.
- A tier whose annual fee is 0.00 USD writes no entry at all.

**Once a year only.** At most one annual fee is billed per account year: where an annual fee already stands on that card account for that statement cycle, no second one is billed.

**The refund window.** When the cardholder closes the account within 30 calendar days after the annual fee posted, the fee is reversed in full as a bank error. After that window it is never refunded and never prorated.

*Illustrations on hypothetical dates.* An account under Personal Credit Cards opened on 14 March carries March as its anniversary month, so the annual fee falls on the statement closing in March each year. On a tier that charges 95.00 USD and does not charge it in the first account year, the March statement closing eleven months after opening carries 0.00 USD and the following March statement carries 95.00 USD. Where an annual fee posted on 3 March and the account closes on 2 April, the closure falls on day 30 of the window and the fee is reversed in full; where it closes on 4 April, the window has passed and nothing is refunded, not even a part for the unused months.
